title: Lab-grown meat and the wall it keeps hitting

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The first approved product went on sale at one restaurant, one day a week, and that's it. Two years later, still one restaurant.

turns.speaker: Lars
turns.text: That tells you it's a demonstration rather than a business.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: The problem is the growth medium. It used to need serum from calf blood, which rather defeats the point, and the replacements are pharmaceutical grade and priced accordingly.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: How far off is it, in cost terms?

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: Orders of magnitude, still. Not a few per cent.

turns.speaker: Lars
turns.text: And scaling isn't a matter of building a bigger tank. Cells need oxygen through the middle of the mass and they don't have a bloodstream to do it.

turns.speaker: Lars
turns.text: Mince for a very long time. Structured meat is a much harder problem than anyone said at the start.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: What I'd question is whether it's even the right target. Plant protein is here, it's cheap, and it's improving faster.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: But it hasn't converted the people who actually eat a lot of meat, and those are the ones who matter.

turns.speaker: Bea
turns.text: That's true, and it's the one argument for cultured meat I can't answer.

turns.speaker: Lars
turns.text: The regulatory politics are turning against it too. Two countries have banned it outright before it existed at scale.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Which is quite the achievement, banning something nobody can buy.

points: Cultured meat has been on sale at a single restaurant one day a week for two years, suggesting a demonstration rather than a business.
Bea explains the growth medium is the core cost problem, with alternatives to calf serum priced at pharmaceutical grade.
Costs remain orders of magnitude too high.
Lars notes scaling is limited because cells need oxygen delivered through the tissue without a bloodstream, so structured cuts are far harder than mince.
Bea questions whether plant protein is the better target, being cheaper and improving faster.
Nikhil's unanswered point is that plant protein has not converted heavy meat eaters; they also note some countries banned cultured meat before it reached scale.
